scheme_name: PMMSY: Establishment of Medium RAS / Biofloc culture system - Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana or PMMSY is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on May 20, 2020. 

The scheme aims to bring about a significant transformation in the fisheries sector. 

It is designed to enhance fish production and productivity in the country. 

The PMMSY focuses on sustainable development and the promotion of modern fishing practices. 

The establishment of Medium Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS) and Biofloc culture systems is one of the key components of this scheme. 

The initiative is particularly relevant for states like Haryana, where aquaculture is being promoted as a viable livelihood option. 

The primary objective of the PMMSY is to increase fish production to 22 million metric tons by 2024-25. 

This target represents a substantial increase from the 13.7 million metric tons produced in 2018-19. 

The scheme also aims to create an additional 55 lakh jobs in the fisheries sector. 

The PMMSY is expected to boost the income of fishers and fish farmers significantly. 

The financial outlay for the PMMSY is approximately INR 20,050 crores. 

Of this, INR 9,800 crores is allocated for the development of inland fisheries and aquaculture. 

The establishment of Medium RAS and Biofloc culture systems falls under the aquaculture development component. 

These systems are designed to enhance fish farming efficiency and sustainability. 

The Biofloc technology promotes the growth of beneficial microorganisms in the water. 

This technology allows for higher stocking densities of fish. 

It also reduces the need for water exchange, making it environmentally friendly. 

The Medium RAS systems provide a controlled environment for fish farming. 

They recycle water and maintain optimal conditions for fish growth. 

The financial assistance provided under PMMSY for establishing these systems can be substantial. 

Farmers can receive up to 60 percent of the project cost as a subsidy. 

For SC/ST and women entrepreneurs, this subsidy can go up to 80 percent. 

The maximum subsidy amount for establishing a Medium RAS or Biofloc system is capped at INR 20 lakhs. 

This means that a project costing INR 25 lakhs could receive a subsidy of INR 15 lakhs for general applicants. 

For SC/ST and women, the subsidy could be as high as INR 20 lakhs for the same project. 

Eligibility for the PMMSY scheme requires applicants to be involved in fish farming. 

Applicants must be at least 18 years old. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required for this scheme. 

However, applicants must demonstrate knowledge or experience in aquaculture practices. 

The application process for PMMSY is straightforward. 

Interested farmers must approach the respective Fisheries Department in Haryana. 

They can obtain the application form either online or offline. 

The required documents include an identity proof, address proof, and a project report. 

The project report should detail the proposed aquaculture system and its financial viability. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the Fisheries Department. 

The department may conduct a site visit to assess the feasibility of the project. 

Upon approval, the subsidy amount will be disbursed to the applicant. 

The disbursement is typically made in installments based on project milestones. 

The first installment is usually released after the project is initiated. 

Subsequent payments are made upon the completion of specific phases of the project. 

The PMMSY also aims to promote the use of modern technology in aquaculture. 

This includes training programs for farmers on best practices in fish farming. 

The scheme encourages the establishment of fish feed mills and hatcheries. 

This is crucial for ensuring a steady supply of quality fish seed and feed. 

The implementation of the PMMSY is overseen by the Department of Fisheries under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry, and Dairying. 

The department is responsible for formulating policies and guidelines for the scheme. 

It also monitors the progress of projects funded under PMMSY. 

In Haryana, the state government plays a vital role in the implementation of PMMSY. 

The Haryana Fisheries Department is the primary agency responsible for executing the scheme at the state level. 

Farmers can contact the Haryana Fisheries Department for assistance and guidance. 

The department provides support in project planning and execution. 

The PMMSY is expected to have a significant impact on the livelihoods of fish farmers in Haryana. 

It aims to promote sustainable aquaculture practices that are environmentally friendly. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of fish as a source of nutrition. 

Fish is a rich source of protein and essential nutrients. 

The PMMSY aligns with the government’s broader goals of enhancing food security and nutrition. 

The initiative is also expected to contribute to the overall economic development of rural areas. 

By improving fish production, it aims to increase the income levels of fishing communities. 

The PMMSY is part of a larger vision to make India a global leader in fisheries and aquaculture. 

The establishment of Medium RAS and Biofloc systems is a step towards achieving this vision. 

The scheme is expected to foster innovation and research in aquaculture practices. 

It encourages partnerships between government, private sector, and research institutions. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive approach to transforming the fisheries sector in India. 

It addresses various challenges faced by fish farmers, including climate change and resource scarcity. 

The focus on technology and sustainability is crucial for the future of aquaculture. 

The PMMSY represents a significant investment in the livelihoods of millions of fishers and fish farmers across the country. 

In conclusion, the PMMSY and the establishment of Medium RAS and Biofloc culture systems in Haryana is a transformative initiative. 

It aims to enhance fish production, create jobs, and promote sustainable aquaculture practices. 

The scheme provides substantial financial assistance and support for fish farmers. 

It is a critical step towards achieving food security and improving the nutritional status of the population.
